lessons.title: Who Is In My Family?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name members of their family and describe a positive feeling about them.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult shares a photo of their own family.
lessons.main_activity: Children discuss who lives in their home/family, sharing one thing they love doing with a family member.
key_questions: Who is in your family?
What do you like doing together?

differentiation.extension: Child describes extended family (grandparents, cousins)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note sensitivity to varied family structures — evidence for PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Class share: one family activity each child enjoys.
lessons.home_link: Talk about your family together tonight.

lessons.title: Describing Family Members
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a family member using at least one descriptive word.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult describes a family member as a guessing game.
lessons.main_activity: Children describe a family member's appearance/personality to a partner using new vocabulary.
key_questions: What do they look like?
What are they like as a person?

differentiation.extension: Use 3+ descriptive words unprompted

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive vocabulary range — evidence for CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Share one describing word learned today.
lessons.home_link: Describe a family member to someone else at home.

lessons.title: Family Fun Run Warm-Up Game
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to move safely at different speeds during a group game.
lessons.starter_activity: Practise moving fast/slow on the spot.
lessons.main_activity: 'Family Fun Run' relay-style game in pairs, changing pace on instruction (walk like grandma, run like a puppy).
key_questions: How does your body feel moving fast? Slow?
Can you change speed quickly?

differentiation.extension: Add direction changes and different movement styles

lessons.assessment_notes: Note control at varying speeds — evidence for PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Cool down stretches, discuss favourite movement style.
lessons.home_link: Play a movement speed game together outside.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'i'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 'i' and blend it into words (sit, pit, tip).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap s,a,t,p sounds.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'i' sound/action; blend new CVC words (sit, tip, pit) using known sounds.
key_questions: What sound is this?
Can you blend s-i-t?

differentiation.extension: Write CVC words independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 'i' and blending.
lessons.plenary: Sing all 5 sounds learned (s,a,t,p,i).
lessons.home_link: Practise blending sit, tip, pit together.

lessons.title: How Many People in My Family?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count and compare the number of people in different families.
lessons.starter_activity: Count children on the carpet as a warm-up.
lessons.main_activity: Children count family members using drawings/photos from home, then compare family sizes with a partner (more/fewer).
key_questions: How many people are in your family?
Who has more people in their family?

differentiation.extension: Compare 3+ family sizes and order them

lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting and comparing accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class bar chart-style visual of family sizes (simple pictogram).
lessons.home_link: Count and talk about family size at home.

lessons.title: Different Types of Families
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recognise that families come in many forms.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at picture books showing varied family types.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss and look at images of different family structures (two parents, single parent, grandparents raising children, same-sex parents, etc.), emphasising love and care as what makes a family.
key_questions: What makes a family a family?
Are all families the same?

differentiation.extension: Child articulates why families can look different but all show love

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding and acceptance of diversity — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Class agreement: 'All families are special.'
lessons.home_link: Talk about other families you know that might look different from yours.

lessons.title: Family Portrait Painting
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to represent family members using paint, choosing colours purposefully.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a portrait painting example.
lessons.main_activity: Children paint a picture of their family, choosing colours to represent hair/clothing purposefully.
key_questions: Who is in your painting?
Why did you choose that colour?

differentiation.extension: Add background detail (home, garden)

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe purposeful colour choice — evidence for EAD.1.
lessons.plenary: Display family paintings and children introduce their family.
lessons.home_link: Show your family painting and talk about it together.

lessons.title: Missing Family: Managing Feelings
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name a strategy for when they miss a family member.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss: 'Do you ever miss someone during the day?'
lessons.main_activity: Introduce comfort strategies (transitional object, thinking of a happy memory, talking to an adult) for missing family during the school day.
key_questions: What helps you feel better when you miss someone?
Who can you talk to if you feel sad?

differentiation.support: Adult offers one strategy to try
differentiation.extension: Child suggests own strategy

lessons.assessment_notes: Note emerging coping strategies — evidence for PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap: 'It's ok to miss someone, and here's what can help.'
lessons.home_link: Talk about a happy memory together before school tomorrow.

lessons.title: Retelling a Family Event
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recount a simple family event in sequence.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult recounts a simple family event as a model.
lessons.main_activity: Children retell a recent family event (trip, meal, celebration) using sequencing words with adult support.
key_questions: What happened first?
What happened after that?

differentiation.support: Adult scaffolds with questions for each part
differentiation.extension: Retell independently in full sentences

lessons.assessment_notes: Note narrative sequencing ability — evidence for CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One or two children share their event with the class.
lessons.home_link: Practise retelling a family story at bedtime.

lessons.title: Making Family Finger Puppets
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use scissors and glue to construct a simple finger puppet.
lessons.starter_activity: Scissor warm-up snipping practice.
lessons.main_activity: Children cut out and assemble simple paper finger puppets representing family members.
key_questions: Which family member is this puppet?
How did you stick it together?

differentiation.extension: Child cuts own shapes and adds details

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe cutting/sticking control — evidence for PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Use puppets for a mini family role-play.
lessons.home_link: Put on a puppet show for your family.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'The Family Book' by Todd Parr
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify a way their family is similar to one shown in the book.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict what the book might be about from the cover.
lessons.main_activity: Read 'The Family Book' (or similar), pausing to discuss similarities/differences to children's own families.
key_questions: Is your family like this page?
What is different about your family?

differentiation.extension: Explain in full sentences with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and personal connection to text — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Class discussion: 'All families are different and all are great.'
lessons.home_link: Read a book about families together.

lessons.title: Sharing Fairly Between Family Members
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to share a small group of objects equally between two people.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what 'sharing fairly' means with an example.
lessons.main_activity: Children practise sharing counters/toys equally between two puppets representing 'siblings', checking it's fair.
key_questions: Is that fair? How do you know?
What if there's one left over?

differentiation.extension: Share 6-8 objects between 2-3 people, discuss remainders

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early understanding of equal sharing — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap what 'sharing fairly' looks like.
lessons.home_link: Practise sharing snacks fairly with a sibling/friend.

lessons.title: Family Photos: Then and Now
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sequence family photos from oldest to newest.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at an old photo of the school/area if available.
lessons.main_activity: (If available) children sequence family photos from different times, discussing changes noticed (hairstyles, clothes, technology).
resources_needed: Family photos from different eras (optional) or provided example photos
key_questions: Which photo is oldest? How do you know?
What has changed?

differentiation.extension: Sequence 3-4 photos and explain reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of chronology — evidence for UTW.1.
lessons.plenary: Share one interesting change noticed in family photos.
lessons.home_link: Look at old family photos together and talk about what's changed.

lessons.title: Family Role-Play Home Corner
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to take on a family role and use imaginative language during play.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss different roles within a family.
lessons.main_activity: Free play in the home corner, taking on different family roles, cooking, caring for baby dolls, and communicating imaginatively.
resources_needed: Home corner resources, dolls, play kitchen items
key_questions: Who are you being? What are you doing?
What would you say to the baby?

differentiation.support: Adult joins play to model language
differentiation.extension: Child initiates and extends the play scenario

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative role-play and social language — evidence for EAD.2/PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Share what roles were played in the home corner today.
lessons.home_link: Play pretend family games at home.

lessons.title: Helping at Home
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one way they help their family at home.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what jobs grown-ups do at home.
lessons.main_activity: Children share/act out a way they help at home (tidying toys, setting table); create a class 'Helping Hands' display.
key_questions: How do you help your family?
Why is helping important?

differentiation.extension: Child explains why their chore helps the family

lessons.assessment_notes: Note sense of responsibility — evidence for PSED.2.
lessons.plenary: Class 'Helping Hands' display unveiled together.
lessons.home_link: Choose one new job to help with at home this week.

lessons.title: Listening to Family Instructions Game
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to follow a family-themed multi-step instruction.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sequencing words.
lessons.main_activity: 'Helping Grandma' game — give 2-3 step instructions themed around helping a family member (e.g. 'pick up the toy, then put it in the box, then sit down') for children to follow.
key_questions: What do you do first?
Can you repeat the instructions back?

differentiation.extension: 3-step instructions repeated back first

lessons.assessment_notes: Record instruction-following level — evidence for CL.1.
lessons.plenary: Children take turns giving instructions to a partner.
lessons.home_link: Practise following 2-step instructions for a chore at home.

lessons.title: Family Piggyback/Wheelbarrow Games (Adapted)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to demonstrate core strength and coordination in a partner physical game.
lessons.starter_activity: Core strength warm-up (plank holds, bear crawl).
lessons.main_activity: Adapted partner games building strength/coordination (bear crawl races, crab walk relay) themed around 'helping a family member move something'.
key_questions: What muscles are you using?
How do you keep your balance?

differentiation.extension: Add an obstacle or increase distance

lessons.assessment_notes: Note core strength and coordination progress — evidence for PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Cool down and discuss which game was toughest.
lessons.home_link: Try a bear crawl or crab walk race at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'n'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 'n' and blend it into words (nap, pin, tin).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap s,a,t,p,i sounds.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'n' sound/action; blend new CVC words (nap, pin, tin, nip).
key_questions: What sound is this?
Can you blend n-a-p?

differentiation.extension: Write CVC words with 'n' independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 'n' and blending.
lessons.plenary: Sing all 6 sounds learned so far.
lessons.home_link: Practise blending nap, pin, tin together.

lessons.title: Family Height Comparison
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to order 3+ objects/people by height.
lessons.starter_activity: Compare heights of two children (sensitively) as an example.
lessons.main_activity: Children order family figure cut-outs (or classroom objects) from shortest to tallest, discussing comparative language.
resources_needed: Family figure cut-outs of varying heights or classroom objects
key_questions: Who/what is tallest? How do you know?
Can you order all three?

differentiation.extension: Order 4-5 items and explain reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note ordering/comparing skill — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of tallest to shortest vocabulary.
lessons.home_link: Compare heights of family members at home (measuring against a wall).

lessons.title: Family Celebrations and Traditions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one family tradition or celebration.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult shares a family tradition example.
lessons.main_activity: Children share a family celebration/tradition (birthday, festival, mealtime ritual) they enjoy, noting similarities and differences across the class.
key_questions: What do you celebrate with your family?
What makes it special?

differentiation.support: Adult prompts with simple choice questions
differentiation.extension: Explain why the tradition is meaningful

lessons.assessment_notes: Note awareness of cultural/family diversity — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Create a class list of different family traditions shared.
lessons.home_link: Ask a family member about a tradition and why it started.

lessons.title: Family Tree Craft
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a simple family tree using craft materials.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at an example family tree picture.
lessons.main_activity: Children create a simple family tree using a tree template, adding leaves/photos/drawings for each family member.
key_questions: Who will you put on your family tree?
Where does this person go?

differentiation.support: Pre-drawn simple tree with 3 leaf spaces
differentiation.extension: Add extended family (grandparents, cousins) with more leaves

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe understanding of family structure and material use — evidence for EAD.1/UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Display family trees and children introduce them.
lessons.home_link: Add a missing family member to your tree with help at home.

lessons.title: Being Kind Like Family
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to demonstrate a kind action towards a classmate.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss kind things family members do for each other.
lessons.main_activity: 'Kindness chain' activity — children perform a small kind act for a partner (helping tidy, complimenting) and add a paper link to a class kindness chain.
key_questions: What kind thing did you do today?
How did it make your friend feel?

differentiation.support: Adult suggests a kind action to try
differentiation.extension: Child identifies and performs their own kind act

lessons.assessment_notes: Note prosocial behaviour — evidence for PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Display the growing kindness chain.
lessons.home_link: Do one kind thing for a family member today.

lessons.title: Interviewing a Partner About Their Family
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to ask a simple question and report back an answer.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult models asking a simple question to a child.
lessons.main_activity: In pairs, children ask each other one prepared question about family (e.g. 'What's your favourite family meal?') and report the answer to the group.
key_questions: What did you ask your partner?
What did they say?

differentiation.support: Adult provides the question to ask
differentiation.extension: Child thinks of their own follow-up question

lessons.assessment_notes: Note question-asking and reporting skills — evidence for CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Class shares interesting answers gathered.
lessons.home_link: Interview a family member with one question and report back tomorrow.

lessons.title: Making a Family Card
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use cutting, folding, and writing/mark-making skills to make a card.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at example greeting cards.
lessons.main_activity: Children make a simple folded card for a family member, decorating and attempting a message/name.
key_questions: Who is this card for?
What message will you write/draw?

differentiation.extension: Fold independently and write a short message

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe fine motor precision in folding/cutting — evidence for PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Children share who their card is for and why.
lessons.home_link: Give your card to the family member it's for.

lessons.title: Writing About My Family
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write a simple label or short phrase about their family.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sounds learned (s,a,t,p,i,n).
lessons.main_activity: Children attempt to write simple family-related words/labels (e.g. 'mum', 'dad', 'sis') using known phonics sounds, with adult support.
key_questions: What sound does 'mum' start with?
Can you write that word?

differentiation.extension: Child attempts independent phonetic spelling

lessons.assessment_notes: Record writing stage progress — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share written words with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Practise writing family members' names together.

lessons.title: Number Bonds Introduction: Making 5 with Family Members
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find different ways to make 5 using two groups.
lessons.starter_activity: Show 5 fingers, hide some, guess how many are hidden.
lessons.main_activity: Using family figure counters, children explore different combinations that make 5 (e.g. 2 adults + 3 children, 4+1) and record with drawings.
key_questions: How many ways can you make 5?
What else could make 5?

differentiation.support: Focus on making 5 with physical counters only
differentiation.extension: Record multiple number bonds to 5 systematically

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early number bond understanding — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class collects all the different ways to make 5 found.
lessons.home_link: Find ways to make 5 using toys or snacks at home.

lessons.title: Homes Around the World
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one way homes can look different around the world.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at images of different homes worldwide (apartment, house, yurt, houseboat).
lessons.main_activity: Discuss and compare different home types found around the world, linking to children's own home types.
key_questions: What does your home look like?
How is this home different from yours?

differentiation.extension: Explain why homes might differ (climate, culture)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note growing awareness of global diversity — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Class discussion: 'All homes are different, but all are special.'
lessons.home_link: Describe your home to a family member and what makes it special.

lessons.title: Family Song Performance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sing a family-themed song with actions confidently.
lessons.starter_activity: Learn a new family-themed rhyme (e.g. 'The Family in the Car').
lessons.main_activity: Practise the song with actions in small groups, then perform for another group/class.
key_questions: What action goes with this line?
How did it feel to perform?

differentiation.extension: Suggest and lead a new action

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence performing and following song structure — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; discuss favourite part of the song.
lessons.home_link: Perform the family song for your own family.

lessons.title: Celebrating Our Families Together
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to express appreciation for their own family.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's family learning.
lessons.main_activity: Children complete 'I am thankful for my family because ___' and share, creating a class 'Family Appreciation' display combining the week's work (portraits, trees, cards).
key_questions: What are you thankful for about your family?
What did you enjoy learning this week?

differentiation.extension: Give 2-3 reasons with elaboration

lessons.assessment_notes: Note emotional expression and reflection — evidence for PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Class 'Family Appreciation' display unveiling.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family you appreciate them this weekend.

lessons.title: Show and Tell: My Family Week Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise what they learned about family this week in sentences.
lessons.starter_activity: Look back through the week's family photos/work.
lessons.main_activity: Circle time: each child shares their favourite family-themed activity from the week using a full sentence.
key_questions: What was your favourite family activity this week?
What did you learn about families?

differentiation.support: Point to a photo, adult scaffolds sentence
differentiation.extension: Give 2-3 sentences with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Compare sentence complexity to Week 1 — evidence of progress for CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Class cheer for a great week of family learning.
lessons.home_link: Share your favourite family activity from this week with your family.

lessons.title: Family Sports Day Mini-Games
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to participate in simple team physical games with control.
lessons.starter_activity: Warm-up jog and stretch.
lessons.main_activity: Mini 'family sports day' games — egg and spoon walk, bean bag throw, simple relay — in small teams.
resources_needed: Spoons, soft eggs/balls, bean bags, cones
key_questions: How did your team work together?
What skill did you use in this game?

differentiation.extension: Add a scoring element or extra challenge

lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 3 PD progress — evidence for PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all teams; cool down together.
lessons.home_link: Have a mini sports day with family at home/park.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: s,a,t,p,i,n
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read simple CVC words using all sounds learned so far.
lessons.starter_activity: Quick-fire flashcard review of all 6 sounds.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations: word-building with magnetic letters, CVC word reading cards, sound-writing practice.
key_questions: Can you build this word?
Can you read this word?

differentiation.extension: Build/read and write 3-sound CVC words independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Finalise week 3 phonics tracker for all sounds and blending/reading ability.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all 6 sounds learned with a phonics song and word reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading simple CVC words together over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Sharing, and Number Bonds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, sharing, and number bond skills learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting family members, sharing fairly between two, number bonds to 5.
key_questions: How many are there?
Is that shared fairly?
What makes 5?

differentiation.extension: Independent completion with recording

lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 3 maths observations for each child.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining counting and number bonds.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising sharing and counting together over the weekend.

lessons.title: Our Class Family Book
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to contribute a page about their family to a shared class book.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at an example class book from a previous topic (or a published one).
lessons.main_activity: Each child completes a page (drawing + adult-scribed sentence) for a shared 'Our Class Families' book, to be kept in the reading corner.
key_questions: What will you draw for your page?
What sentence do you want written?

differentiation.extension: Child attempts to write part of the sentence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note engagement and quality of contribution — evidence for UTW.2/LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Read the completed class book together.
lessons.home_link: Share the class family book page with your own family when it's sent home to look at.

lessons.title: Family Celebration Dance and Song
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to perform a learned song/dance confidently as part of a group.
lessons.starter_activity: Warm-up with a favourite dance from earlier in the week.
lessons.main_activity: Perform the week's family song with actions/dance as a whole-class celebration of the family topic.
key_questions: What was your favourite part of the performance?
How did it feel to perform with everyone?

differentiation.extension: Lead an action or verse

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment in group performance — evidence for EAD.2/PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; recap the fun week of family learning.
lessons.home_link: Perform the song/dance for your family this weekend.
